title: Government and law
description: Words for policy, regulation, crime, punishment and public spending in Task 2 essays.

words.definition: a law or a set of laws made by a government
words.example: New legislation requires all new buildings to include solar panels.

words.definition: to control an activity by rules
words.example: Governments should regulate the amount of sugar in children's food.

words.definition: to make sure that people obey a law or rule
words.example: Speed limits are useless unless the police enforce them.

words.definition: something that discourages people from doing something
words.example: There is little evidence that harsher sentences act as a deterrent to crime.

words.definition: helping someone return to a normal life after prison, illness or addiction
words.example: Education in prisons supports the rehabilitation of offenders.

words.definition: a person who has committed a crime
words.example: Young offenders may benefit more from community service than prison.

words.definition: to commit another crime after being punished
words.example: Prisoners who learn a trade are less likely to reoffend.

words.definition: a person who pays taxes
words.example: Building a new stadium would cost taxpayers billions.

words.definition: to pay part of the cost of something to make it cheaper
words.example: Many governments subsidise public transport to reduce traffic.

words.definition: money provided by the government
words.example: The arts depend heavily on public funding in many countries.

words.definition: to officially forbid something
words.example: Several countries have banned smoking in all indoor public places.

words.definition: to officially force a rule, tax or punishment on people
words.example: The city imposed a fee on drivers entering the centre during rush hour.

words.definition: responsible for your actions and expected to explain them
words.example: Politicians must be held accountable for how public money is spent.

words.definition: dishonest or illegal behaviour by people in power
words.example: Corruption reduces public trust in government institutions.

words.definition: the basic rights of people, such as freedom of speech
words.example: Mass surveillance raises serious concerns about civil liberties.

words.definition: help given by the government to people in need
words.example: Some argue that generous welfare payments discourage people from working.

words.definition: the basic systems a country needs, such as roads, power and water
words.example: Investment in infrastructure creates jobs and supports economic growth.

words.definition: to give money or resources for a particular purpose
words.example: A larger share of the budget should be allocated to primary education.

words.definition: the punishment given by a court
words.example: He received a two-year prison sentence for fraud.

words.definition: unpaid work in the community given as a punishment instead of prison
words.example: Community service allows minor offenders to repay society without losing their jobs.

words.definition: a strong official action to stop illegal activity
words.example: The police launched a crackdown on illegal street racing.

words.definition: relating to young people who are not yet adults
words.example: Juvenile crime is often linked to poverty and school dropout.

words.definition: a set of ideas or a plan of action agreed by a government or organisation
words.example: The government's housing policy has failed to make homes affordable.

words.definition: the people or organisations with official power
words.example: Local authorities are responsible for collecting household waste.

words.definition: the act of obeying a rule or law
words.example: Regular inspections ensure compliance with safety standards.

words.definition: to make something allowed by law
words.example: Some countries have legalised street vending in designated areas.

words.definition: complicated official rules and processes
words.example: Excessive bureaucracy discourages people from starting new businesses.

words.definition: to become involved in a situation to change what happens
words.example: Governments sometimes need to intervene when markets fail.

words.definition: punishment by death
words.example: Opponents argue that capital punishment does not reduce violent crime.

words.definition: openness about decisions and activities
words.example: Publishing budgets online increases transparency in local government.
